classification.difficultyReason: Match single and double parallel marks and name their line pairs.

inlines.text: Name the pairs of parallel lines in these diagrams.

spec.description: Two separate parallel segments rising gently to the right, with italic endpoint labels and matching single arrowheads toward their right ends.
spec.mathematics: QR and ST are parallel. Each has one up-right parallel mark. No endpoint dots or numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: The geometry and marks are supplied; the symbolic answer is hidden from the question.

answer.worked: $QR\parallel ST$. The two lines have matching parallel-arrow marks.

spec.description: AB and CD rise to the right with matching single arrows. PQ slopes down-right and crosses AB before CD. All six endpoint labels are italic.
spec.mathematics: AB is parallel to CD; PQ is a transversal. Intersections are unlabelled.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied geometry and parallel marks remain visible; the completed symbolic response is answer evidence only.

answer.worked: $AB\parallel CD$. These lines have matching parallel-arrow marks; $PQ$ crosses both.

spec.description: Two shallow down-right lines cross two steep down-right lines. A and B are the upper intersections; C and D are the lower intersections. Labels sit below-left. All lines extend beyond the intersections.
spec.mathematics: AB is parallel to CD (matching double arrows); AC is parallel to BD (matching single arrows). The two distinct direction families are intentionally distinguished, correcting the source single-arrow reuse while preserving the supplied pair answers.
spec.answerVisibility: Preserve supplied marks without adding right-angle symbols or revealing the symbolic answers.

answer.worked: $AB\parallel CD$ and $AC\parallel BD$. The upper and lower lines form one parallel pair; the two steep lines form the other.
